target_customer: Businesses, retailers, game companies and individuals who need video editing or production and hire freelancers
problem: Buyers with raw footage found it slow and costly to hire a good video editor or producer; Videopixie lets them post a project and receive bids.
business_model: Marketplace take rate on video production projects

founders.name: Thomas Escourrou
founders.background_notes: Named as a founder in TechCrunch June 2013; the YC page lists only Saffell.

competitors.name: Viedit
competitors.what: Marketplace of freelance editors who cut customers' footage

technical_complexity.rationale: A bidding marketplace with file transfer and payments is standard web engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Liquidity of creators and repeat buyers helps, but general freelance sites such as Fiverr and Upwork also sell video editing.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent bought or copied it in sources found; the product is still live under TT Labs Inc.

market_need_then: TechCrunch in 2013 described a marketplace for people with raw footage and freelance editors, and in 2015 said projects ranged from 1,000 to 10,000 dollars with over 1,000 creators on the platform.

identity.voice_and_tone: Direct marketplace copy: Find videographers, directors, video editors, and animators

brand_strength.rationale: The playful name suggests a helper for editing, but the product grew beyond editing to full production and sources show no press about the brand, merch or community.

pivots.from: Sellstage (the founders' earlier YC S11 company)
pivots.to: Videopixie, a marketplace for video editors
pivots.why: Not stated in sources; TechCrunch 2013 says the founders were in YC S11 with Sellstage and launched Videopixie in June 2013

outcome_analysis: The founders came into YC S11 with Sellstage and launched Videopixie in June 2013 as an editor marketplace. By May 2015 they reported over one million dollars in gross volume, more than 1,000 creators and a 1.1 million dollar seed from Jawed Karim and 500 Startups, with the scope widening to full video production. The site is still live in 2026 under the entity TT Labs Inc, suggesting a small steady business rather than a breakout.
notes: Founding year conflicts: YC and Latka 2011, TechCrunch 2015 says 2013. The 2014 seed round with ACE & Company, FundersClub, Orange Fab and Linden Mobile Ventures rests on a single database (CB Insights, which shows 40K total and may include placeholder data) seen only in a search snippet; amount is unknown. The 1.1M seed in May 2015 is from TechCrunch with a second listing on Seedtable and Village.ai. YC Start Fund involvement is mentioned with no amount in 2013. Competitor sourced to June 2013 launch coverage, two years after the S11 batch; as_of is set to the 2013 launch. The website footer shows Copyright 2026 TT Labs Inc., not explained. Dated competitor list is limited to Viedit; Fiverr and Upwork are listed as incumbents from a later comparison page, not as dated competitors. The 2014-02 seed was removed from rounds in this audit: it has no amount, comes from CB Insights alone (a placeholder entry, 40K total) and no outlet reports a 2014 round; a second aggregator lists a June 2014 seed with FundersClub and no amount, which does not corroborate it. Seedtable and TechCrunch support only the 1.1M seed of May 2015.
